text:
maria: Ran an nsys capture on the latest wrapper/scheduler changes. seeing a ~12% tail increase for 2k token runs. attaching quick summary below.

kevin: ugh, great. where is the time going? scheduler or engine?

maria: main hotspots look like:
- Wrapper::invoke CPU spin (Scheduler handoff) ~9%
- Scheduler::dispatch enq path ~7%
- TRTInfer::enqueue short kernels (setup/param copy) ~6%
- cudaMemcpyAsync host->device spikes during kv prefetch ~5%
- vLLM::kv_cache_lookup CPU locked sections ~4%
(total adds up to the regression)

raj: can you paste the nsys timeline snippet? even a flame ascii helps.

maria: pasted snippet from nsys (trimmed):
```
Time(ms) | Activity
0-2      | accept/deserialize (cpu)
2-8      | Wrapper::invoke (cpu)  - spin/wait
8-15     | Scheduler::dispatch -> TRTInfer::enqueue (cpu->gpu handoff)
15-250   | kernel: attention_fwd_trt (gpu)
250-255  | cudaMemcpyAsync(kv_prefetch)
255-520  | kernel: attn_kv_update (gpu)
520-540  | Wrapper::postprocess (cpu)
```

maria: note the intermittent cudaMemcpyAsync at ~250ms aligning with cache prefetch for longer contexts. that wasn't present in older traces.

emma: did the scheduling change add any synchronous fences or extra stream syncs?

maria: we added a fallback path that ensures KV prefetch completion before enqueue for correctness under some race. suspect that path triggers memcopy+stream sync for some shards.

kevin: can we change to a non-blocking prefetch + stream-capture fences? or postpone until after enqueue where possible?

raj: two concerns: correctness + memory pressure. if we defer prefetch until after enqueue we might increase page faults or stall exec. need a safe experiment.

perf-bot: perf regression alert triggered: +11.8% p95 latency for generate endpoint since deploy 2026-03-12. Baseline run id: 2119999999. New run id: 2123456789.

maria: plan: 1) instrument wrapper to log fast-path vs fallback path counts, 2) run targeted nsys with stream names and trace markers around KV prefetch, 3) try toggling fallback off in canary.

kevin: add a small microbenchmark: repeat 1k/2k context lengths, measure cudaMemcpyAsync sizes and stream usage. if memcopy sizes are tiny but frequent we should coalesce.

emma: also check kernel selection change from last runtime PR: kernel variant A vs B; variant B reduces kernel time but increases setup overhead. possible tradeoff.

maria: good call — nsys shows we switched to kernel variant B for 1024+ sequence, which has more parameter setup in enqueue (extra small kernels), explain the TRTInfer::enqueue uptick.

raj: suggested quick experiments:
- revert scheduling fallback (dev flag) and rerun perf tests
- force kernel variant A and measure overall latency and GPU utilization
- instrument kv cache path to batch cudaMemcpyAsync calls (coalesce by request window)

kevin: I'll own the kernel variant A/B flip test. maria, can you add the logs for fallback counts?

maria: on it. will push a dev flag and a short repro script. sharing initial results in this thread.

perf-bot: note: if we revert fallback we must create an automated equity test to ensure regressions don't reintroduce race. add test to eng-runtime/e2e.

maria: ack. timeline: aim for canary toggle + nsys run by EOD. if we see revert -> perf back to baseline, we'll MTR the fallback implementation.

kevin: thanks. small ask: can we also capture kernel occupancy report (nsys + nvprof) so we can compare A vs B occupancy? might explain throughput vs setup cost.

maria: yes, nvprof occupancy export queued. will attach CSV and a short note.

emma: flagging this for postmortem if we don't fix next deploy; the regressed p95 is affecting customers. :warning:

raj: cool. next steps captured. I'll help review the rollback patch if needed.

maria: thanks all — starting trace now and will post artifacts (nsys, nvprof occupancy, short flame) here.

kevin: :thumbsup:
